evidence_types.analytical_truth: Exact or hand-computable scientific quantity from a small declared problem.
evidence_types.independent_implementation_equivalence: Same estimand/specification represented or fitted independently from the package code path.
evidence_types.simulation_recovery: Known data-generating parameters assessed for recovery under finite stochastic sampling.
evidence_types.cross_implementation_sensitivity: Related external implementation used to assess sensitivity when smoothing, discretization, covariance, scoring, or other contracts cannot be made exactly equivalent.

entries.dataset_problem: Four mean-zero curves X_i(t)=a_i phi(t) on an irregular three-point grid with unit functional norm for phi.
entries.expected_result: lambda_1 equals sample variance of a_i; absolute weighted inner product with phi equals 1; one-component reconstruction is exact.
entries.comparison_metric: eigenvalue, sign-invariant weighted inner product, reconstruction
entries.limitations: Rank-one analytical case; it does not by itself validate sparse/PACE or near-tied eigenspaces.

entries.dataset_problem: Repeated synthetic participant/trial functions with the same explicitly declared degree-1 fixed/random bases and REML specification.
entries.expected_result: Package fit and separately assembled stacked MixedLM agree for the same likelihood and covariance parameterization.
entries.tolerance: fixed parameters rtol=1e-8; random covariance rtol=1e-7; scale/log-likelihood 1e-8 to 1e-9
entries.limitations: Independent design assembly but the same established statsmodels optimizer/backend; nested trial covariance is not covered by this row.

entries.reference_source: independently assembled direct statsmodels.GEE exposure fit
entries.dataset_problem: Repeated Poisson counts with explicit time-varying exposure and degree-1 coefficient basis.
entries.expected_result: Direct stacked GEE and package fit agree; rate is exp(eta_rate), expected count is exposure*rate.
entries.tolerance: coefficients rtol=1e-9; covariance rtol=1e-8; fitted functions rtol=1e-10
entries.limitations: Validates the working-independence marginal exposure contract, not alternative GEE correlation structures.

entries.reference_source: row-expanded Bernoulli observations fitted directly with statsmodels.GEE
entries.dataset_problem: Grouped success counts plus explicit denominators expanded into individual Bernoulli rows under the same participant clustering.
entries.expected_result: Weighted grouped representation and row-expanded Bernoulli representation agree.

entries.limitations: Small path; validates recurrence semantics/tie-independent optimum rather than large-scale performance.

entries.expected_result: symmetric1 raw=1; symmetric2 raw=1; normalization denominator=5; normalized=0.2.
entries.limitations: Does not validate every Sakoe-Chiba window configuration.

entries.dataset_problem: Three recurrence points forming one diagonal line of length 3 and no qualifying vertical line.
entries.expected_result: RR=3/16, DET=1, Lmean=Lmax=3, diagonal entropy=0, LAM=0.
entries.tolerance: exact counts; zero relative tolerance for derived ratios
entries.limitations: Uses the package's explicitly documented finite-border convention; other software may use different RQA conventions.

entries.dataset_problem: Five-sample binary source/target construction with four effective transitions, each local contribution equal to 1 bit.
entries.expected_result: TE=1 bit and every local contribution=1 bit.
entries.comparison_metric: direct count-formula result versus package TE
entries.tolerance: absolute tolerance 1e-15 for base-2 logarithm arithmetic
entries.limitations: Empirical plug-in discrete TE only; does not validate causal interpretation or continuous-state estimators.

entries.dataset_problem: Repeated participant trial functions generated in the fitted degree-1 basis.
entries.expected_result: Recovered functions remain within predeclared finite-sample absolute recovery bands.
entries.tolerance: atol=0.12 intercept; atol=0.08 condition in existing truth test
entries.limitations: Finite seeded simulation evidence; weaker than analytical truth or independent implementation equivalence.

entries.dataset_problem: Repeated Poisson functional counts generated from declared log-link coefficient functions.
entries.expected_result: Estimated coefficient functions recover generating functions within predeclared stochastic bounds.
entries.limitations: Seeded finite-sample recovery, not an external implementation comparison.

entries.reference_source: analytically constructed rank-two quadrature-weighted covariance operator
entries.dataset_problem: Known rank-two covariance assembled from weighted-orthonormal functions on a finite quadrature grid.
entries.expected_result: Recovered eigenvalues equal the generating values and absolute weighted component similarity/orthonormality equal one up to numerical precision.
entries.comparison_metric: eigenvalue allclose, sign-invariant weighted similarity, weighted Gram matrix
entries.tolerance: rtol=1e-10 and atol between 1e-10 and 1e-12 as encoded in test
entries.limitations: Validates weighted eigendecomposition independently of mean/covariance smoothing and PACE score recovery.

entries.reference_source: private known-truth two-component sparse functional generator
entries.dataset_problem: Irregularly sampled curves generated from known mean, two eigenfunctions/eigenvalues, latent scores, and Gaussian measurement noise.
entries.expected_result: Recovered functional subspace and latent scores meet predeclared finite-sample recovery thresholds while raw sparse trajectories remain uninterpolated.
entries.comparison_metric: weighted component/subspace similarity, score correlation, finite score diagnostics
entries.tolerance: weighted similarities >0.80; score correlations >0.75 and >0.55 in the seeded baseline test
entries.limitations: Favorable seeded recovery case; broader stress/failure evidence is generated separately by the sparse-native-validation workflow.

entries.dataset_problem: Same finite pooled x/y observations, evaluation points, degree, kernel, and numerical bandwidth supplied to both local-linear smoothers.
entries.expected_result: Matched one-dimensional local-linear fitted values agree to tight floating-point tolerance.
entries.platforms: optional FDApy sparse CI on Python 3.11-3.12
entries.limitations: Primitive smoother equivalence only; it does not imply equivalence of the full covariance or PACE estimator.

entries.dataset_problem: Same sparse observations and shared evaluation grid with aligned local-polynomial bandwidth/kernel/degree where possible.
entries.expected_result: No exact equality claim; broad invariant guards should exclude catastrophic cross-implementation disagreement.
entries.comparison_metric: principal cosines, absolute weighted component similarity, finite relative eigenvalue differences, sign-aligned score correlation/RMSE
entries.tolerance: minimum principal cosine >0.60, component similarity >0.45, score correlation >0.35; eigenvalue differences/RMSE must be finite
entries.platforms: optional FDApy sparse CI on Python 3.11-3.12
entries.limitations: Not equivalence. FDApy uses radial 2-D LP covariance smoothing, its own noise rule, interpolation before irregular PACE, and a covariance reconstructed from retained eigencomponents; native eyetrajectoriespy uses a product kernel, explicit noise contract, native observation times, and the full fitted covariance surface.

scientific_quantity: latent covariance diagonal used for diagonal-difference measurement-noise estimation
45-degree rotated local polynomial intercept on the covariance diagonal
entries.reference_source: Yao, Müller & Wang (2005) PACE diagonal construction plus an exactly representable rotated local-polynomial test surface
entries.dataset_problem: Off-diagonal covariance products generated exactly from a function linear along the rotated diagonal coordinate and quadratic perpendicular to it.
entries.expected_result: The rotated covariance-diagonal smoother recovers the exact diagonal intercept function to numerical precision.
entries.comparison_metric: pointwise fitted diagonal versus exact analytical diagonal
entries.tolerance: rtol=1e-11; atol=1e-11 in the exact local-polynomial test
entries.limitations: Validates the source-faithful diagonal smoother algebra; it does not imply universal finite-sample accuracy of the difference-based measurement-noise variance estimator.

entries.method: Native sparse multivariate FPCA + joint PACE
entries.dataset_problem: Irregular paired x/y trajectories from known vector means and vector-valued eigenfunctions over rho_xy=-0.6,0,0.3,0.6,0.9, plus one directional asymmetric-Cxy design and one correlated measurement-error design.
entries.expected_result: All seven native qualification cases satisfy the predeclared finite-sample guards; covariance is assessed by named blocks, rho_xy=0 is assessed with tied-eigenspace geometry and Procrustes-aligned scores, and supplied measurement error is not misreported as estimated recovery.
entries.comparison_metric: mean ISE relative to analytic finite-sample sampling reference; named covariance-block ISE; joint principal cosines/angles; separated score correlation/RMSE; tied-eigenspace Procrustes score RMSE; reconstruction ISE; score failure/conditioning; PSD correction
entries.tolerance: guards encoded in scripts/run_sparse_mfpca_recovery_validation.py; mean ISE scaled to sum(lambda)/n; sensitivity grids/ridges are descriptive and do not select tuning parameters
entries.platforms: dedicated Ubuntu Python 3.12 sparse-mfpca-recovery workflow plus core cross-platform unit tests
entries.limitations: Seeded finite-sample native recovery. The true measurement-error covariance is supplied to the estimator rather than estimated. Two-stage and mGSFPCA cross-implementation sensitivity, observation-loss stress, and 0.12 performance qualification are separate later evidence.

entries.method: Native direct sparse MFPCA versus internal two-stage marginal sparse-basis benchmark
entries.reference_source: validation-only two-stage construction from separate native x/y sparse FPCA/PACE bases and empirical covariance of concatenated marginal scores
entries.dataset_problem: Same deterministic irregular rho_xy=0.6 planar fixture, declared marginal ranks 1 and 2, true diagonal measurement-error variances supplied to both marginal fits and the canonical direct fit.
entries.expected_result: No architecture winner or automatic rank selection claim; invariant subspace/score agreement should remain finite while covariance and reconstruction evidence characterize the information lost under marginal truncation.
entries.comparison_metric: named covariance-block ISE; truth/direct functional-subspace principal cosines; truth/direct score-subspace principal cosines; latent reconstruction ISE; finite-score fraction
entries.tolerance: descriptive sensitivity only; outputs must be finite where defined, declared ranks must be exactly 1 and 2, automatic_rank_selection=false, architecture_winner_selected=false
entries.platforms: dedicated Ubuntu Python 3.12 sparse-mfpca-comparator-sensitivity workflow plus core unit tests
entries.limitations: Internal benchmark, not a second public estimator. Empirical joint score covariance depends on finite-sample marginal PACE scores. Rank-1 truncation deliberately cannot represent the complete truth; no winner is selected from this fixture.

entries.method: Native direct sparse MFPCA versus mGSFPCA 0.2.2
entries.reference_source: CRAN mGSFPCA 0.2.2 spMultFPCA on the same frozen irregular rho_xy=0.6 native/truth fixture
entries.dataset_problem: Thirty irregular paired x/y curves on a shared truth grid with explicit four-component target and persisted original-ID to integer-ID comparator adapter.
entries.expected_result: No exact equivalence claim; native/truth, mGSFPCA/truth, and mGSFPCA/native invariant subspace relationships are all retained and finite without automatic architecture selection.
entries.comparison_metric: functional-subspace principal cosines; score-subspace principal cosines; descriptive retained eigenvalues
entries.tolerance: descriptive invariant sensitivity; exact equivalence is explicitly false and no architecture winner is selected
entries.platforms: Ubuntu 24.04, Python 3.12, R release, exact mGSFPCA 0.2.2
entries.limitations: Not equivalence. Sparse smoothing, likelihood, marginal truncation, basis construction, normalization, and score contracts differ. mGSFPCA is validation-only and not a runtime dependency.
